newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean shares end higher in volatile trading.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean shares end higher in volatile trading.

text.p: Shares ended Wednesday's trading slightly higher after fluctuating for most of the day, trapped in a tug of war between profit-takers and bargain hunters, brokers said.
The index rose 6.58 points to a provisional close of 835.19, after ranging between 823.68 and 835.26. Advancing shares beat decliners 518 to 394.
"I think this pattern will continue tomorrow, as shares fluctuate of short-term profit-taking," said Dongbang Peregrine Securities broker Don Lee.
Brokers said overall market energy was still strong. Volume remained healthy, with 47.67 million shares changing hands.
Individual counters with good earnings prospects performed well. LG Metals rose 700 won to 20,600, and Nasan Industries gained 1,600 won to its upper limit of 28,600 won.
Some paper stocks were active throughout the day. Brokers said South Korean paper firms would benefit from large stockpiles of pulp now that global pulp prices had risen.
Shinho Paper rose 360 won to 8,700 in active trading.
The four initial public offerings which began trading on Wednesday ended at their limit highs.
AUK Corp's shares ended up 4,500 won to 79,500. Hyundai Housing gained 1,000 won to 18,000, Dong Yang Elevator rose 2,100 won to 37,100, while Korea Electronic climbed 3,600 won to 63,600.
Brokers said hopes for an interest rate cut and the inflow of funds from an employee stock scheme would keep the market sentiment bouyant despite the consolidation.

Beginning October 21, a stock investment savings scheme sweetened with tax benefits for white-collar workers will be launched. The government has said it anticipated about two trillion won to come into the market through this plan.
